implementation_notes: install(ContentNegotiation) registers one converter per Content-Type (json(), xml(), cbor(), protobuf(), or a custom ContentConverter) and call.respond(model) serializes the same @Serializable data class into whichever representation the Accept header requests; the converter registry is therefore the view registry and the plugin is the negotiation point. HTML comes from call.respondText/respondHtml or a template engine (kotlinx.html, Twig/TemplateFlow), and no per-format View object exists. Suspend-based handlers make the per-representation work explicit, which is useful when one representation (PDF) is far more expensive than the others.
pitfalls: When several converters are installed and the client sends */* or no Accept header, the first installed converter produces the response, so 'everything came back as XML' is a registration-order issue.
kotlinx.serialization encodes only declared properties of @Serializable types: a field present in the HTML template but absent from the DTO disappears from the API silently.
Serializing the persistence entity couples the wire format to the schema; keep a DTO per representation, especially when the entity has lazy-loaded relations.
